annotations.title: Faith is.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> By this deſcription of faith, and by all the commendation therof through the whole chapter, you may vvell perceiue that the Apoſtle knewe not the forged ſpecial faith of the Proteſtants, vvhereby euery one of theſe new Sectmaſters & their folovvers beleeue their ſinnes are remitted, and that them ſelues ſhal be ſaued, though their ſectes be cleane contrarie one to an other.

notes.text: Not only or a special faith.

annotations.title: Not appearing.
annotations.text: ◦ This is the praiſe of faith, ſaith S. Auguſtine, if that which is beleeued, be not ſeen. For vvhat great thing is it, if that be beleeued, which is ſeen? according to that ſentence of our Lord when he rebuked his diſciple, ſaying: Becauſe thou haſt ſeen me Thomas, thou haſt beleeued: bleſſed are they that haue not ſeen and haue beleeued. Aug. in euang. Io. tract. 79. Which may be a rebuke alſo and a checke to al thoſe faithles ſpeaches, I would ſee him, taſt him, touch him and feele his very fleſh in the Sacrament, othervviſe I wil not beleeue.

notes.text: Faith is of things not seen: as in the B. Sacrament.

annotations.title: He that commeth.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Faith is the foundation and ground of all other vertues and worſhip of God, vvithout which no man can pleaſe God. Therfore if one be a Iewe, a Heathen, or an heretike, that is to ſay, be without the Catholike faith, al his workes ſhal profit him no whit to ſaluation.

notes.text: Nothing profitable or meritorious without faith,

annotations.title: Adored the toppe of his rod.
annotations.text: [1] The learned may ſee here that the Apoſtle doth not tie him ſelf to the Hebrew in the place of Geneſis [2] whence it is alleged, but folovveth the Septuaginta, though it differ from the Hebrew, as alſo the other Apoſtles and Euangeliſts and our Sauiour himſelf did: neither vvere they curious (as men now a days) to examine all by the Hebrew only, becauſe they vvriting and ſpeaking by the Holy Ghoſt, knevve very well that this tranſlation [3] is the ſenſe of the Holy Ghoſt alſo, and as true, and as directly intended as the other: and therefore alſo that tranſlation continued always authentical in the Greeke Church, notwithſtanding the diuerſitie thereof from the Hebrew. Euen ſo vve that be Catholics, folow vvith all the Latin fathers the authentical [4] Latin tranſlation, though it be not always agreable to the Hebrew or Greeke that now is. But Caluin is not only very ſaucie, but very ignorant, vvhen he ſaith that the Septuaginta were deceiued, and yet that the Apoſtle without curioſity vvas content to folow them: becauſe it is euident, that [5] the Hebrew being then without points, [6] might be tranſlated the one way as vvel as the other. Vvhich they vnderſtood ſo vvel (and therefore vvere not deceiued) that within three lines after, in the beginning of the next chapter, they tranſlate the ſame vvord, as he vvould haue it in this place. [7] Againe obſerue in thoſe words, He adored the toppe of his rod, that adoration (as the Scripture vſeth this word) may be done to creatures, or to God at and before a creature: as, at or [8] before the Arke of the Teſtament in old time, now at or before the crucifixe, relics, images: and in the Pſalms 98. 131. Adore ye his footſtool. Adore ye toward his holy mount. We will adore tovvard the place where his feete ſtoode: or (vvhich by the Hebrew phraſe is all one) Adore ye his holy mount. We will adore the place where his feete ſtood. as alſo [9] the Greeke Fathers, S. Damaſcene li. 1. de imaginibus, and Leontius cited of him, yea S. Chryſoſtom alſo do handle theſe places, and namely that of the Apoſtle vvhich vve now ſpeake of, interpreting the Greeke as our Latin hath, and as we do, He adored the rod or the toppe of his rod, that is, the ſcepter of Joſeph now Prince of Ægypt, ſo fulfilling Ioſephs dreams which foretold the ſame Gen. 37: and vvithal ſignifying as it vvere by this propheticall fact, [10] the kingdom of Iſrael or of the ten tribes that was to come of Joſeph by Ephraim his younger ſonne in the firſt king Jeroboam, thus the Greeke Fathers. Vvherevnto may be added, that all this vvas done in type and figure of Chriſt's ſcepter and kingdom, whom he adored by and in his Croſs, as he did Joſeph by or in his rod and ſcepter: and therefore the Apoſtle ſaith, he did it by faith, as hauing reſpect tovvard things to come. By all vvhich it is euident, that it is falſe vvhich the Caluiniſts teach, that vve may not adore image, crucifixe, or any viſible creature, that is, we may not adore God at or by ſuch creatures, nor kneele before them: and therefore their [11] corrupt tranſlation of this place for the ſame purpoſe is intolerable, ſaying thus, (Leaning) vpon his ſtaffe he adored (God). adding no leſſe then tvvo words more then is in the Greeke. Which though it might be the ſenſe of the place, and S. Auguſtine ſo expoundeth it, yet they ſhould not make his expoſition the text of holy Scripture, ſpecially whereas he only of all the ancient Fathers (as Beza confeſſeth) ſo expoundeth it.

notes.text: The citations in the new Testament, not only according to the Hebrue, but to the Septuaginta.
Adoration of creatures, and namely of holy things.

annotations.title: Wrought iuſtice.
annotations.text: [1] Men are not iuſt by beleefe onely, as the Proteſtants affirme, but by working iuſtice. And vve may note that in all this long commendation of faith in the fathers and holy perſons, their good workes are alſo ſpecially recounted, as Rahabs harbouring the ſpies, Abrahams offering his ſonne (vvhich their vvorkes S. Iames [2] doth inculcate:) Noës making the Arke Gen. 6. Abels better oblation then Cains Gen. 4. & Hebr. 11. v. 4. and ſo forth. therfore S. Clement Alexandrinus ſaith, [3]that the ſaid perſons and others vvere iuſt by faith and obedience, by faith and hoſpitality, by faith and patience, by faith and humility. ◦ The Apoſtles purpoſe then is nothing els, but to proue to the Hebrues (vvho made ſo great account of their Patriarches and forefathers and their famous actes) that all theſe glorious perſonages and their vvorkes vvere commendable and acceptable onely through the faith they had of Chriſt, vvithout vvhich faith none of all their liues and workes ſhould haue profited them any whit: the Gentiles doing many noble actes (as Heretikes may alſo doe) vvhich are of no eſtimation before God, becauſe they lacke faith. And that is the ſcope of S. Paules Epiſtle to the Romanes, and of al other paſſages where he commendeth faith: further prouing ſpecially in this Epiſtle to the Hebrues, that all their ſacrifices vvere nothing els but figures and atteſtations of the Chriſtian faith in Chriſt and his death. Al vvhich high reſolution & concluſion againſt the Iewes and Gentiles, that the Chriſtian faith is the true faith & religion, the Heretikes of our time ignorantly and brutiſhly abuſe againſt Chriſtian workes, ſacrifice, and Sacraments, which the Apoſtle meant ſpecially to commend and eſtabliſh by his high commendation of the faith in Chriſt.

notes.text: No workes of the Patriarkes or any other profitable, but by their faith in Christ. Which is alwaies the Apostles meaning in commending faith.

annotations.title: Without vs ſhould not.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The fathers before Chriſt could not be accompliſhed, that is, not admitted to the heauenly ioyes, viſion, and fruition of God, till the Apoſtles and other of the new law vvere aſſociate to them, and the vvay to euerlaſting glorie opened by our Lordes death and Aſcenſion. Neither ſhal either they or vve be fully perfected in glorie both of body and ſoul, till the general reſurrection: Gods prouidence being ſo, that vve ſhould not one be conſummated vvithout an other, all being of one faith, and redeemed by one Lord Chriſt.

notes.text: The Patriarkes and other iust not in heauen before Christ.
